children: is facing renewed investor pressure after comments from CEO Kelly Ortberg triggered a sharp pullback, but Bank of America said the market reaction may have gone too far. The firm kept its Buy rating and $270 price target in a Friday note.

Shares fell 3.7% Wednesday after Ortberg said Boeing still had work to do before consistently reaching its 737 MAX production goal of 47 aircraft a month. He pointed to delays in wing production and said the company needs more time to stabilize output.

BofA analyst Ronald Epstein said Boeing's recovery is unlikely to move in a straight line. He also noted that the company's operating position has improved from a year earlier, while its supply network remains capable of supporting higher production.
Boeing also faces regulatory scrutiny. The Federal Aviation Administration proposed inspections for certain 737 MAX aircraft after reports of cracks near a forward galley door structure.
Separately, BofA identified a potential SPEEA labor strike as a near-term risk, with the current contract set to expire Oct. 6.

title: Boeing Stock Plunges After CEO Warning: BofA Calls It an 'Overreaction'
